correctness.rationale: The simple-cycle hypothesis n >= 3 makes the two adjacent columns distinct. Each column has at most two selected vertices by independence on C5. An empty column forces both adjacent columns to contain every row; a singleton at row r forces both adjacent columns to contain the adjacent rows r+2 and r-2. Both are impossible. Write each independent pair uniquely as {t-1,t+1}; disjoint adjacent pairs have centers differing by +1 or -1 modulo 5. The unselected rows t+2 and t-2 each require a neighbor from the adjacent column with the corresponding center t+1 or t-1. Thus the two neighboring centers are opposite steps from t, and every consecutive increment is the same. Closure is equivalent to 5 dividing n. Conversely, this recurrence supplies the required outside neighbors, including two within the column at t; the first center and first step distinguish the ten labelled sets. The official 2016 paper uses matching graph and kernel definitions. An independent exact witness check, `python3 /workspace/branches/replay_2_3.py`, verifies the ten distinct C5 x C10 sets, each with 20 selected vertices of inside-degree zero and 30 outside vertices of inside-degree 2 or 4. The all-n conclusion is analytic, not extrapolated from this check. Inspected the two frozen checker sources without executing them.
